QF.id: XIII Introduction to Forwards and Futures_21

question.text: If the spot price of a stock is Rs 500, the risk-free rate is 10% per annum, and the stock pays a dividend of Rs 15 in 2 months, what is the theoretical 3-month futures price?

explanation.text: The Logic: Cost-of-carry with a known cash dividend: F = S(1 + r x t) - D(1 + r x remaining) = 500 x (1 + 0.10 x 3/12) - 15 x (1 + 0.10 x 1/12) = 512.50 - 15.125 = Rs 497.38, i.e. about Rs 497.4. The dividend reduces the fair futures price because the futures holder does not receive the dividend. The Trap: Rs 512.50 ignores the dividend entirely; Rs 485.00 subtracts the dividend from spot without carrying it forward; Rs 500 wrongly equates futures to spot. Note: A continuous-compounding or PV-dividend version yields a very similar value (about Rs 497.5); the small difference reflects the compounding convention.
